input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day on us for "any delay in providing a dependency" — a Customer-payable penalty with no materiality threshold, no grace period and no aggregate cap, triggered by minor breaches. This fails both the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees), and the "any delay" trigger plus unbounded daily accrual sits in walk-away territory. The mutual cap in § 21.1 does not cure it: it caps aggregate liability but leaves the LD mechanic intact and could still expose us to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000, and the § 7.3 dispute-withholding right addresses invoiced amounts, not the penalty itself. No other Customer-payable LD or termination penalty appears in the document. Redline deletes the daily LD and gives Vendor schedule relief instead.

proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable per-day liquidated damages with schedule relief for Vendor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, so we have removed the USD 25,000 per day charge for dependency delays; our playbook position is that no liquidated damages are payable by Customer. Instead, Vendor receives an equitable extension of affected timelines, which addresses the underlying delay risk.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: If Customer delays in providing a dependency, Vendor's sole and exclusive remedy shall be an equitable extension of the affected timelines. No liquidated damages, penalty or similar payment shall be payable by Customer under this Agreement.
